description: Advertisement consent for the installation of 1No. BT Street Hub Unit and associated advertisement panels on either side of the unit
decision_conditions: <p><span style="font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The proposed StreetHub, by reason of its size, scale, detailed design, and illumination featuring a moving digital display, would result in an obtrusive and visually incongruous feature that contributes to an unsightly proliferation and clutter of signage and street furniture in the conservation area that would fail to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the Clapton Square Conservation Area. As such, the proposal would be contrary to policies D3 (Optimising site capacity through the design-led approach), D4 (Delivering good design), D8 (Public realm), and HC1 (Heritage conservation and growth) of the London Plan (2021) and policies PP1 (Public Realm), PP8 (Hackney Central and Surrounds), LP1 (High Quality Design), LP3 (Designated Heritage Assets), and LP7 (Advertisements) of Hackney's Local Development Plan LP33 (2020), the </span><span style="font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Public Realm Strategy SPD (2012) and Hackney's Commercial Extensions and Alterations SPD (2026).</span></p>

<p><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">The proposed StreetHub fails to contribute to a safe shared pedestrian and cycle way. The introduction of a large digital advertisement introduces unnecessary distraction and a physical obstruction on the public footpath, contrary to highway safety. Furthermore, reducing the footpath width in an area that already contains several items of street furniture reduces the pavement available for the free flow of pedestrians and cyclists without obstruction, harming the quality and safety of the walking/cycling environment. As such, the proposal would be contrary to policies D8 (Public realm) and T2 (Healthy streets) of the London Plan (2021) and policies PP1 (Public Realm), PP8 (Hackney Central and Surrounds), LP7 (Advertisements), LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods), and LP42 (Walking and Cycling) of Hackney’s Local Development Plan (2020).</span></p>
